title: Security cooperation commitments depend on a workforce that is still being counted, trained, and staffed
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107976 review of the Department of Defense Security Cooperation Workforce Development Program
geography: United States and overseas U.S. security-cooperation organizations; DOD workforce provisions and partner-capacity activities

observations.period: As of May 2026; FY2024 NDAA workforce provisions

denominator.unit: security-cooperation workforce provisions GAO identified for analysis under 10 U.S.C. section 384

completed_provisions.unit: provisions for which GAO found DOD work complete

human_capital_completed.unit: of 36 Human Capital Initiative provisions completed

human_capital_in_progress.unit: of 36 Human Capital Initiative provisions in progress

human_capital_not_started.unit: of 36 Human Capital Initiative provisions not started

planned_completion.unit: DSCA estimate for completing remaining workforce tasks

observations.method: GAO reviewed DSCA documents and interviewed officials responsible for workforce provisions; GAO classified provisions as complete, in progress, or not started based on evidence available as of May 2026.
observations.uncertainty: A provision classified complete is an implementation-status judgment, not proof that the workforce has sufficient capacity, that training changed field performance, or that partner capabilities improved.
observations.subgroup: DSCA teams, the Human Capital Initiative, overseas security-cooperation organizations, the Defense Security Cooperation University, the FMS Center of Excellence, and related DOD components.
observations.counterinterpretation: Formal certification, workforce coding, and phased reforms can improve professionalization even before all tasks are complete; a long implementation horizon does not by itself imply failed security cooperation.

observations.period: October 2025–April 2026; identified positions and staffing constraints

denominator.unit: security-cooperation workforce positions DSCA identified across nine functional areas as of October 2025

fms_center_vacancies.unit: approximately five of 15 FMS Center of Excellence positions reported unfilled

sco_positions.unit: Security Cooperation Organization functional-area positions in DSCA data; distinct from 1,320 SCO personnel cited in a different workforce count

research_grants.unit: DSCU Young Institute grants awarded in FY2024, plus one cooperative agreement

observations.method: GAO reviewed DSCA workforce data and implementation documents and reported official explanations of staffing and research-capacity challenges.
observations.uncertainty: Position counts are not filled-person counts, and the report uses different scopes for workforce positions and SCO personnel. Staffing gaps do not directly measure partner outcomes, end-use monitoring quality, or operational readiness.
observations.subgroup: DOD civilian and military personnel, overseas security-cooperation organizations, FMS Center of Excellence staff, training and research personnel, and support enablers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Some unfilled positions may be temporary or intentionally managed through other personnel, contractors, or existing expertise; reported shortfalls identify capacity risk, not a quantified mission failure.

related_sources.claim: Official GAO report supplies workforce-provision status, position counts, certification, staffing, training, and research-capacity findings.

boundary: This record establishes an institutional workforce and professionalization stage beneath U.S. security cooperation. It does not establish partner capability, equipment delivery, end-use compliance, alliance trust, deterrence, battlefield effect, or external behavior.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO accessible HTML report retrieved and hashed; underlying DOD personnel systems, workforce survey, partner records, and operational assessments not retained
